hunt:mobile-session.area: Mobile child session, tokens and homework capture (apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts, runtime.ts, family-view.ts; apps/mobile/src/homework/**; packages/contracts/src/auth.ts; apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts)

findings.title: A refresh whose response is lost after the server rotated the token unpairs the paired device as refresh-token theft
findings.mechanism: refresh() persists the rotated refresh token only from the response body. On any non-401 failure it rethrows and deliberately keeps the OLD refresh token (line 135-136: "Offline or server trouble: keep the refresh token so the device reconnects later"). But POST /v1/child/refresh commits the rotation inside one transaction (apps/api/src/routes/child-auth.ts:230-231: issueRefreshToken + `set used_at = ...`), so if the response is lost after that commit — the client's own 20s DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS in packages/contracts/src/client.ts, a wifi/cellular switch, a Worker evicted after commit — the device keeps a token the server has already marked used_at. The next refresh presents it and hits the theft branch (child-auth.ts:205-213), which revokes the whole child_session, writes audit action 'child_session.revoked_token_reuse', and answers 401. The client's own 401 handler then calls forget() -> unpairChildDevice(), deleting the refresh token and profile. The comment's stated reasoning is wrong for exactly this interleaving: keeping the old token does not let the device reconnect later, it guarantees the pairing is destroyed. Refresh happens ~4x/hour per tablet, so one dropped response on a flaky home network ends the pairing.
findings.repro: Pair, let the access token lapse, make one child call whose /v1/child/refresh request reaches the server (rotation commits) but whose response never arrives (NETWORK), then make one more child call on a good connection.
findings.proof: PROBE B in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/hunt-r4/mobile-child/probes.probe.ts drives the real createChildSession against a mock that mirrors child-auth.ts. Printed: server log ['pair','refresh:committed_then_response_lost','refresh:THEFT_REVOKED','data:401 /v1/child/me'], sessionRevoked true, 'PROBE B still paired? false', and STORAGE_KEYS.childRefreshToken gone from storage. So the child is told "Ask a grown-up to connect this device again" and a parent has to mint a new pairing code, over one lost HTTP response.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the server a short reuse grace instead of treating every re-presentation as theft: private.child_refresh_tokens already has replaced_by, so in the `row.used_at` branch, when used_at is within a small window (e.g. 60s) and the replacement token has not itself been used, re-issue the access token for that replacement (returning the same replaced_by token) rather than revoking the session; revoke only outside the grace or when the replacement was already consumed. Optionally also record 'rotation in flight' on the device so the client can tell a lost rotation from a genuinely dead session.

findings.title: The child's rewards and help/report screens get no token retry, so the MOB-R2-02 recovery is missing on the surface that carries safety reports
findings.mechanism: withChildTokenRetry was applied to only two of the four child clients: apps/mobile/src/family/runtime.ts:45 and apps/mobile/src/homework/child-api.ts:18. The child's rewards screen (apps/mobile/app/(child)/rewards.tsx:44) and the child's help/report screen (apps/mobile/app/(child)/help.tsx:29) build `createMobileApi(tokenSource)` straight from the source registered in apps/mobile/src/lib/app-session.ts:51-52, which is `childSession.accessToken` with no wrapper. When the device clock moves backwards after a token was received — the exact state MOB-R2-02 was written for, where the cached token is dead server-side but the device still believes it live — these screens get 401 and nothing invalidates the cached token, so EVERY subsequent tap presents the same dead token. help.tsx maps UNAUTHENTICATED to CHILD_HELP_COPY.notConnected (apps/mobile/src/privacy/child-help.ts:88) and the report is not queued anywhere, so the child's attempt to report a problem is silently dropped while the homework screens in the same app recover on their first try. The screens stay broken for the whole remaining device-clock lifetime of the stale token (up to CHILD_ACCESS_TTL_SECONDS = 900s plus the backwards jump).
findings.repro: Pair; advance real time past the access-token lifetime; move the device clock back 30 minutes; tap a report choice on the child Help screen three times.
findings.proof: PROBE C in the scratch probe file. Printed: 'PROBE C bare attempt 1/2/3: UNAUTHENTICATED, refreshes=0' and server log ['pair','data:401 /v1/child/reports' x3,'data:401 /v1/child/me','refresh:ok','data:200 /v1/child/me'] — the bare client never triggers a refresh, the wrapped client recovers on its first call at the same instant.
findings.suggestedFix: Register the wrapped client, not the raw token source: have app-session.ts hand rewards/privacy a client (or a token source plus the retry) built once via withChildTokenRetry(createMobileApi(childSession.accessToken), childSession), or export the single wrapped childApi and have both screens use it, so the rule holds on every child surface rather than two of four.

findings.title: withChildTokenRetry gives the whole session one retry slot, not one per call: a second call refused at the same moment is told the device is not connected
findings.mechanism: `once` decides whether to retry by `session.invalidateAccessToken()`, which returns true only if a token was cached AT THAT MOMENT (child-session.ts:189-193). Two calls that both presented the same stale token race: the first 401 to land invalidates (true) and retries; the second finds `access === null`, gets false, and rethrows UNAUTHENTICATED even though the device is paired and the refresh that is already in flight would have served it. The predicate answers "is there a cached token" when the question is "did the call I just made present a token that is no longer current". Reachable without any explicit Promise.all: an in-flight request from a screen the child just navigated away from still resolves into `once` (apps/mobile/app/(child)/results.tsx:47-56 only sets `active=false`, the request keeps running), so the scan list's 401 can consume the slot and the scan-detail request the child is looking at fails; likewise the limits GET issued on scan-screen mount (apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:99, failure swallowed) can consume it and make the child's POST /v1/assignments fail with "Ask a grown-up to connect this device again", so the scan is not sent.
findings.repro: Pair; advance past the token lifetime; move the device clock back 30 minutes; issue two child calls concurrently through childApi.
findings.proof: PROBE A in the scratch probe file. Printed: statuses ['fulfilled','rejected'], reasons ['ok','connect again'], server log ['pair','data:401 /v1/child/me','data:401 /v1/child/assignments','refresh:ok','data:200 /v1/child/me'] — one call recovered, the other was told the device is not connected while isPaired() was still true.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the retry decision per call rather than per session: have the wrapper capture the token it presented (e.g. accessToken() returns it, or invalidateAccessToken(presented) only clears when it matches) and retry once whenever the failed call presented a token AND the cached token is now different-or-absent. The existing single-flight refresher already collapses the concurrent refreshes, so both calls then get the fresh token and only one /v1/child/refresh is made.

findings.title: The parent's device list still says "Connected" for a child device whose session ended any way except logout or a parent action
findings.mechanism: The round-3 fix (API-AUTH-R2-05) stamps child_devices.revoked_at only in the logout handler (child-auth.ts:259-267). The parent's list derives connectedness purely from that column — GET /v1/family/devices selects only child_devices rows (apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:429) and apps/mobile/src/family/family-view.ts:130 renders `d.revokedAt ? 'Disconnected' : 'Connected'` — so every other way a session ends leaves the tablet listed as Connected for good. Two such paths remain: (a) the refresh-token-reuse revocation at child-auth.ts:207, which HUNT4-MOB-1 shows is reachable from an ordinary lost response, and (b) natural expiry, since app.current_child_id() requires `s.expires_at > now()` (supabase/migrations/0001_core_identity.sql:363) while nothing stamps the device when CHILD_REFRESH_TTL_SECONDS (30 days) elapses on an unused tablet. In both cases the child sees "Ask a grown-up to connect this device again" while the one screen the parent would check to find out reports the device as Connected, with a live "Disconnect" button and no hint that a new pairing code is what is needed. Deletion, archive, consent withdrawal and parent revoke all do stamp the device, so this is the one-surface-fixed shape rather than a missing feature.
findings.repro: Pair a device, trigger the reuse revocation (present a rotated refresh token twice, as PROBE B does), then GET /v1/family/devices as the parent: the row still has revokedAt null. Same for a session whose expires_at has passed.
findings.proof: Read of the three files above; PROBE B shows the reuse revocation firing from a plain network fault. child-auth.ts:207 updates child_sessions only — grep over apps/api/src for child_devices confirms the only writers are guardians.ts:726 (consent), family.ts:399/453 (archive, parent revoke), child-auth.ts:123 (insert) and child-auth.ts:260 (logout).
findings.suggestedFix: Either stamp child_devices in the reuse branch too (and when a session is found expired), or better, stop deriving "Connected" from child_devices alone: have GET /v1/family/devices report per-device session liveness (exists a child_session with revoked_at is null and expires_at > now()) and let family-view.ts say "Needs a new connect code" for a device whose sessions have all ended, so no future revoke path can silently lie to the parent again.

findings.title: cancelScan's 'too_late' answer is discarded, so a child who stops a scan the server already accepted is told it stopped and is set up to send it twice
findings.mechanism: upload.ts:276-290 computes three distinct outcomes for cancelScan ('cancelled' | 'nothing_to_cancel' | 'too_late', the last from BUSINESS_RULE INVALID_TRANSITION) precisely so the caller can tell the child the truth. Both call sites throw the value away: scan.tsx:126 (`void cancelScan(...).catch(() => undefined)`) and scan.tsx:275, where the abort path then unconditionally sets `upload = {kind:'error', message: 'Stopped. Your pages are still here.'}` and resets attemptRef to a fresh createKey/finalizeKey (scan.tsx:276). If the child taps "Stop sending" while the finalize request is in flight, `cancellable` turns the aborted response into ScanCancelledError (upload.ts:126-134) even though the server committed the finalize. The cancel that follows normally succeeds because 'queued' is in CANCELLABLE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES, but once the scan job has moved it out of 'queued' the cancel is refused with INVALID_TRANSITION (apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1066-1073) and returns 'too_late'. The child is then told the scan was stopped when it is being checked and charged, and because the idempotency keys were rotated, "Try again" creates a SECOND assignment for the same homework — two jobs and two page-allowance charges against AC_CAPTURE_06's one-job-one-charge.
findings.repro: Child taps "Stop sending" during the POST /v1/assignments/{id}/finalize round trip, and the scan job picks the assignment up out of 'queued' before the cancel POST lands; then tap "Try again".
findings.proof: Read of apps/mobile/app/(child)/scan.tsx:272-286, apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts:255-290, apps/api/src/routes/homework.ts:1060-1080 and packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:149-171 (CANCELLABLE excludes extracting/checking/verifying, FINALIZED includes queued). No test exercises the 'too_late' branch of either call site.
findings.suggestedFix: Branch on the cancelScan result in scan.tsx: on 'cancelled' keep the current copy and the fresh attempt; on 'too_late' keep the SAME attempt (so "Try again" re-creates with the same createKey and is reported as already sent via the FINALIZED_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES path) and tell the child the scan was already on its way, e.g. "That one was already sent — check My scans."

checkedSound: Device-clock lifetime arithmetic (child-session.ts:97-110, 140-148): receivedAt captured with deps.now() AFTER the response arrives (refresh line 128, pair line 165) and BEFORE the two storage writes, so expiresAtMs is conservative. accessTokenExpiresInSeconds = deps.config.childAccessTtlSeconds (child-auth.ts:57) is the same TTL issueChildAccessToken uses for the JWT exp (apps/api/src/auth/child.ts:20-21, which floors issuedAt so serverExp <= now+ttl); receipt latency is bounded well under EXPIRY_SKEW_MS=30s against a 900s default TTL. A constant clock offset in either direction is now harmless — I re-ran the round-3 tests for -20/+20 minute skews and they hold.

Single-flight refresher cannot present the same refresh token twice: refresh() awaits persist() (which writes the rotated token to storage) before resolving, and `inflight = null` runs in the .finally() after that, so a second refresh() always reads the new token. No second child token source exists: grep over apps/mobile for createMobileApi/createApiClient shows every child client built from childSession.accessToken, and app-session.ts remains the only registrar (L-007 holds).

withChildTokenRetry retries at most once and never loops: after forget() the cached token is null so invalidateAccessToken() returns false; a refusal with no cached token, and a refusal on the retry, are both passed through (verified by the round-3 tests plus my probes). It forwards `options` (signal, timeoutMs) unchanged on the retry, so uploadScan's AbortSignal still stops a retried create/register/finalize, and all retried calls are idempotent (idempotencyKey on create/finalize).

Upload resume and idempotency (apps/mobile/src/homework/upload.ts): a NETWORK failure during finalize keeps the same attempt, and the retry's POST /v1/assignments with the same createKey returns the existing assignment whose status is now 'queued', which is in FINALIZED_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES, so it is reported as sent instead of re-registering pages or double-charging. Memory discipline (one page's bytes at a time), the byteSize re-check in sendPage, and the pre-API homeworkScanFits/HOMEWORK_IMAGE_LIMITS checks all still hold.

The failed_final copy change is honest and the claim in its comment checks out: apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.tsx:125-145 really does carry per-errorCode advice for SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS, AI_PAUSED_TOO_LONG and FORMAT_NEEDS_CONVERSION, and no error code reaches the child screen. The results screen's "Scan again" button keys off the unchanged title string 'Let’s try a new scan' (results.tsx:143), so round 3 did not break it — brittle, but not a defect today.

The new logout SQL (child-auth.ts:253-268) is correct as written: child_sessions.expires_at is NOT NULL (0001_core_identity.sql:328) so the `not exists` liveness test cannot go three-valued; the session is revoked first so it is excluded from its own guard; and both statements use the DB clock now(), matching app.current_child_id(). requireChild re-checks app.current_child_id() on every call, so the still-valid JWT stops working the instant the device row is revoked. (The 'shared tablet, second live session' case the comment describes cannot arise — /pair always inserts a new child_devices row — but the guard is harmless.)

Contract changes are consistent end to end: accessTokenExpiresInSeconds is required and only child-auth.ts's tokenResponse produces childTokenResponseSchema (both /pair and /refresh go through it); unlockSeconds is required and apps/api/src/routes/adult.ts:199 sends it, and all three consumers (apps/mobile/src/family/unlock.ts:78, apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:243, apps/web StepUpPrompt/SecurityPage) parse the same strict schema. unlockSeconds is actually used on mobile (enterParentMode in src/lib/mode.ts:139-141 measures the window on the device clock).

Child privacy and leak guards in the capture/results path: the child DTO carries no answer key (findForbiddenKeys fail-closed at results.tsx:118), flagged answers replace hints and the score line with the reviewed safety notice without naming the kind of concern, no raw server text reaches the child (childUploadMessage/childLoadMessage/CHILD_REPORT_ERRORS map codes and rules only), and the child scan list is bounded (CHILD_LIST_LIMIT, homework.ts:1421).

The biometric owner binding (runtime.ts:83-107): save() refuses without a signed-in parent and writes the owner key before the enabled flag, so a partial write reads as off; signOutParentOnDevice and signOutClosedAccountOnDevice both clear it. isEnabled() also DELETES the enrollment whenever parentAuth.userId() comes back null (e.g. supabase getSession failing to refresh while offline), which costs the parent a re-enrolment — but unlock.ts:30-32 states the fail-closed intent explicitly and the behaviour is consistent with MOB-R2-06, so I am not reporting it.

GET /v1/family/devices returns every child_devices row with no cap; rows accumulate one per pairing (each /pair inserts a new device) and are now all left visible as 'Disconnected'. Bounded by parent-issued pairing codes, so not an unbounded response in practice.

useChildModeOnFocus in apps/mobile/app/(child)/_layout.tsx calls enterChildMode, which does router.dismissAll() + replace('/(child)/home'). I checked whether this can drop a scan in progress: the only entry to the parent area from a child screen is the "Grown-ups" button on (child)/home (scan.tsx's GatedButton only opens device Settings), so backing out of the parent area lands on child home and no page list or in-flight upload is lost.

hunt:mobile-lock.area: Mobile parent-area lock, modes and navigation (apps/mobile: src/lib/mode.ts, app-session.ts, parent-auth.ts, src/family/unlock.ts, runtime.ts, ui.tsx, app/_layout.tsx, app/(parent)/**, app/(child)/**)

findings.title: Locking the parent area on a paired child tablet leaves mode 'parent' and strands the device on the PIN screen; a relaunch shows the parent/child chooser instead of the child's space
findings.mechanism: The new lockParentAreaOnDevice (mode.ts:65-71) is now the action behind both Lock buttons (ui.tsx:LockParentAreaButton) and the backgrounding handler (app-session.ts:74-78). It does four things: forgetParentUnlock, clearAdultCaches, resetNavigationToUnlock, relockOnServer. It never looks at STORAGE_KEYS.childRefreshToken and never touches the persisted mode, so on a device that holds a child pairing it (a) navigates to /(parent)/unlock — modeEffects.resetNavigationToUnlock, runtime.ts:138-143, does router.dismissAll() (a POP_TO_TOP that the root stack's StackRouter serves, see expo-router 57 build/global-state/router.js:83-88 and canDismiss at :110-125) then router.replace, so the child-space route below is popped off and the unlock screen becomes the only route; the unlock screen (app/(parent)/unlock.tsx:138-215) has no 'Back to my space' control, and with one route in the (parent) stack the native header shows no back arrow while the root Stack has headerShown:false (app/_layout.tsx:15) — and (b) leaves pl.mode = 'parent', so entryRoute('parent', paired, …, null) returns null (src/lib/entry.ts:13) and the next cold start of the child's tablet shows the parent/child chooser, not the child space. That is exactly the MOB-R2-04 symptom the sign-out path was fixed for (mode.ts:168-185 writes 'child' and calls resetNavigationToChildHome when a pairing exists) and the MOB-R2-05 rule the child layout enforces (ui.tsx:useChildModeOnFocus). Of the three ways out of the parent area, only the new lock fails to restore child mode on a paired device.
findings.repro: Paired family tablet (pl.child.refresh set). Parent taps Grown-ups → PIN → parent home (pl.mode='parent'). Parent taps 'Lock parent area' (or just sends the app to the background, app-session.ts:68-79). Screen becomes 'Parent area / Enter your 6-digit parent PIN'. Child picks up the tablet: no on-screen way back to their space (iPad: only the edge-swipe, the very thing MOB-R1-07 says a child cannot rely on; Android Back on a single-route root stack exits the app). After the app is killed or relaunched, index.tsx reads mode 'parent' and shows the 'I'm a parent / Connect a child's device' chooser instead of the child home.
findings.proof: Scratch vitest (now at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/hunt-r4/mobile-lock/lock-paired-tablet.scratch.test.ts) driving the real mode.ts + entry.ts: after enterParentMode then lockParentAreaOnDevice on a storage that holds pl.child.refresh, effects.calls === ['clear','unlock','relock'] (no 'child-home'), currentMode(storage) === 'parent', entryRoute('parent',true,true,null) === null while entryRoute('child',true,true,null) === '/(child)/home'. Ran `npx vitest run … --reporter=default` → 1 passed. The file was then moved out of the repo; `git status --porcelain` is empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Give lockParentAreaOnDevice the storage the way signOutParent has it: when STORAGE_KEYS.childRefreshToken exists, write mode 'child' and call resetNavigationToChildHome (the child space needs no PIN; the parent PINs back in from Grown-ups); otherwise keep the current unlock-screen behaviour. As a minimum, add a 'Back to my space' button to app/(parent)/unlock.tsx whenever a child pairing exists, so the lock cannot leave a child on a PIN field with no exit.

findings.title: The unlock screen silently deletes the parent's stored biometric PIN whenever the signed-in user id cannot be read (offline with an expired access token)
findings.mechanism: biometricOffer (src/family/unlock.ts:25-33) folds three different states into one value: a DIFFERENT parent, a PIN with no recorded owner, and 'nobody signed in' all return 'other_user' (line 31). runtime.ts:90-93 then treats 'other_user' as a reason to DESTROY the secret: clearBiometricPin() deletes the SecureStore PIN plus pl.parent.biometricEnabled and pl.parent.biometricOwner (runtime.ts:70-74). parentAuth.userId() (src/lib/parent-auth.ts:122-126) returns null whenever getSession() yields no session — not only when nobody is signed in. In @supabase/auth-js 2.116 __loadSession refreshes an expired access token and, when that refresh fails, returns {data:{session:null}, error} unless the access token is still inside its real expiry window (GoTrueClient.js:2568-2590). So an offline device whose access token has passed expires_at reports 'no signed-in parent', and the enrolment of the parent who is still signed in is deleted. Nothing is shown to the parent; the screen just stops offering Face ID, and re-enrolling is impossible until the device is online again because save() throws without a user id (runtime.ts:97-99).
findings.repro: Parent enables 'Use Face ID or fingerprint next time' (PIN stored, owner recorded). Later, in airplane mode and more than the access-token TTL (1h by default) after the last refresh, they open the app and tap Grown-ups. app/(parent)/unlock.tsx:63-65 runs biometricPinStore.isEnabled() on mount (the effect is declared above the `if (!api)` early return, so it runs even with no usable session) → userId() null → biometricOffer({enabled:true, ownerUserId:'user-a'}, null) === 'other_user' → clearBiometricPin(). The keychain PIN and both flags are gone for good; the parent types the PIN and, once online, has to re-enrol.
findings.proof: Code path read end to end; the deleting branch is the one the round's own test pins: apps/mobile/src/family/screens-r2.review.test.ts:98 asserts biometricOffer({enabled:true, ownerUserId:'user-a'}, null) === 'other_user'. supabase-js behaviour confirmed by reading node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+auth-js@2.116.0/node_modules/@supabase/auth-js/dist/main/GoTrueClient.js:2568-2590 ('const accessTokenStillValid = …; return this._returnResult({ data: { session: null }, error })'). No mobile test covers the runtime store, so nothing catches it.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the unknown case from the mismatch: return a third outcome ('unknown') for signedInUserId === null and have isEnabled() just return false for it — fail closed without deleting. Delete only when a different user id is actually signed in, plus the existing deletes on sign-out and account closure (runtime.ts:174). The legacy ownerUserId === null case can stay a delete if that migration cost is wanted.

findings.title: Signing out is hidden from a child on the unlock screen, but 'Turn off biometric unlock' is left beside the PIN field
findings.mechanism: unlock.tsx:204-212 hides 'Lock parent area' and 'Sign out' unless a live unlock brought the parent here, with the stated reason 'never beside the PIN field, where a child could reach them'. The 'Turn off biometric unlock' button (lines 188-198) is rendered on the same screen with no such gate: its only condition is canBiometric && biometricOn. It calls biometricPinStore.clear(), which deletes the keychain PIN and both flags — a destructive, parent-only setting change performed with no PIN, no OS prompt and no confirmation.
findings.repro: Paired tablet, parent has Face ID unlock enabled. Child taps 'Grown-ups' on the child home (app/(child)/home.tsx:108-113) → /(parent)/unlock. isEnabled() is true (same parent signed in), so the child sees 'Turn off biometric unlock' and taps it. findings.title: A sign-out that supabase-js refused is reported as success: the refresh token stays in localStorage while the portal navigates to /sign-in
findings.mechanism: `async signOut(scope = 'local') { closeRecovery(); await auth.signOut({ scope }); }` throws away the `{ error }` that supabase-js returns, and supabase-js does not reject. In @supabase/auth-js 2.116.0 `_signOut` (dist/module/GoTrueClient.js) starts with `_useSession`; when `__loadSession` finds the stored access token past EXPIRY_MARGIN it tries a refresh, and if that refresh fails at the fetch level with the access token genuinely expired it returns `{ data: { session: null }, error }`. `_signOut` then hits `if (sessionError && !isAuthSessionMissingError(sessionError)) return this._returnResult({ error: sessionError })` and returns BEFORE `removeCurrentSession()` — the session, including its refresh token, is left in localStorage and no /logout request is ever sent, so the refresh token is still valid server-side. SignOutControl.tsx:36-41 then does `try { await auth.signOut('local'); } finally { setBusy(false); void navigate('/sign-in', { replace: true }); }` — no catch, no check that `currentSession()` is now null, and the navigation happens unconditionally. Nothing on screen contradicts it: /sign-in is not a portal path (App.tsx:160) so the 'Signed in as p•••@…' line is not rendered there, and SignInPage.tsx never redirects a still-signed-in visitor — it just shows the sign-in form. This defeats exactly the threat SignOutControl.tsx:8-12 was written for ('On a shared family, school or library computer the next person could read the family's children, homework scans, verdicts, points, safety reports, devices and guardian emails, because read screens need no PIN').

Nothing sensitive is auto-retried, the PIN is cleared from state before the request, and the return path travels as history state through safeNextPath on the Security page (SecurityPage.tsx:214-217).

findings.title: The child PATCH form always sends all three fields, so it silently reverts the other guardian's grade change — the opposite of what its own comment claims
findings.mechanism: EditChildForm's doc comment (ChildrenPage.tsx:392-395) says "Only the fields the parent changed are sent, so a concurrent edit by the other guardian is not overwritten wholesale." The code does the opposite: `submit` always builds `{ nickname, gradeLevel, ageBand }` from its initial-state-seeded inputs (lines 422-426) and sends all three. The API applies every present field (`coalesce(${body.gradeLevel ?? null}::int, grade_level)` in apps/api/src/routes/family.ts). So guardian A opens the edit form while the child is in grade 3, guardian B saves grade 4, then A corrects only the nickname → the grade goes back to 3 with no warning. The grade is what practice generation is pitched at, which is the harm WEB-R2-03 set out to fix. EditFamilyForm (FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:170-178) has the same shape for displayName/timezone.
findings.repro: Two tabs (or two guardians) on /app/children with Riley in grade 3. Tab 2: Edit profile → grade 4 → save. Tab 1 (still showing grade 3): Edit profile → change only the nickname → save. The PATCH body carries gradeLevel 3 and the API writes it, dropping the grade bump.

findings.title: PIN reset drops an owner's aal2 session whenever the factor lookup is slower than the parent's password submit
findings.mechanism: WEB-R2-08 adds a two-step re-verification step, but it is gated on state filled by an unawaited effect: `useEffect` calls `account.assuranceLevel()` and `account.verifiedTotpFactorId()` and only then sets `twoStepFactorId` (PinResetPage.tsx:24-37). The password form reads that state at submit time — `if (outcome.ok) setStep(twoStepFactorId ? 'two_step' : 'pin')` (line 60). `verifiedTotpFactorId()` is a network call (supabase-auth.ts:288, `auth.mfa.listFactors()`). If it has not resolved when the parent submits (autofill + Enter, slow network, or a transient failure taking the `() => undefined` rejection branch), the flow goes straight to the PIN step, the password grant's new aal1 session replaces the aal2 one, the warning paragraph is never shown, and the two-step form is never rendered afterwards (the effect's only dep is `account`, and `step` is already 'pin'). Every /admin page then refuses with "Owner administration requires an MFA session" — exactly the failure this change was written to prevent.
findings.repro: Owner at aal2 opens /app/security/reset-pin and submits the autofilled password before listFactors returns.
findings.proof: Scratch test (<scratchpad>/hardening/hunt-r4/web-portal/pin-reset-race.test.tsx) with `verifiedTotpFactorId()` returning a promise released only after the password click and `assuranceLevel()` = 'aal2' printed: `reached PIN step without two-step? true`, `two-step field present? false`, `PIN reset sent? 1`, `verifyTotp calls: 0`.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the check a resolved precondition rather than a race: hold the lookup in a three-state value ('checking' | factorId | null), disable or relabel "Confirm it's you" while it is 'checking', and re-run the decision after the sign-in (or await the lookup inside onSubmit before signInWithPassword). Handle the rejection branch explicitly instead of silently treating it as "no two-step".

findings.title: An expired download link shows "That download link expired" and "Your download link is ready." at the same time
findings.mechanism: `fetchLink` stores the success outcome "Your download link is ready." in `action.outcome` and sets `link`. The expiry timer then sets `link = null` and `expired = true` (lines 611-624). findings.title: The download link's expiry is the server's instant compared against the browser clock, so a skewed clock keeps a dead link clickable

The comment above it claims "the page can never offer a URL that would answer with the storage service's error document", but a device clock five minutes behind gives remaining ≈ 360 s, so the "Download file" anchor stays on screen and clickable for five minutes after the signature died — exactly the outcome WEB-R2-07 was written to prevent. A clock ahead of the server drops a perfectly valid link immediately.
findings.repro: Set the device clock 5 minutes slow, request a link, wait 90 s, click "Download file" → the storage provider's error document, while the page still says "link valid until …".
findings.proof: Read of PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:605-624 against apps/api/src/routes/export-download.ts (DOWNLOAD_URL_SECONDS = 60, `expiresAt` derived from the server clock); there is no clamp and no local-elapsed measurement anywhere in the component.

findings.title: A child-scope deletion leaves the child's paid slot assigned; activate on a sibling then tells the parent to buy capacity they already pay for, and no route can free it
findings.mechanism: public.request_deletion (migration 0840, the current definition) archives the child and revokes its sessions/devices/jobs/assignments but never touches public.child_slot_assignments — only the purge (app.purge_family_data, 0620/0710/0820) deletes those rows. Meanwhile family.ts:359-368 decides capacity from `count(*) from child_slot_assignments where released_at is null` against family_capacity.paid_slots. So while the deletion is `requested`/`processing` the freed child still occupies a paid slot. Both routes that could release it are now closed: POST /children/:id/activate goes through the new visibleChild() and answers 404 for that child (family.ts:349), and POST /children/:id/archive only releases the slot inside `if (child.status !== 'archived')` (family.ts:392) — request_deletion already set the status to 'archived', so the whole release block, including `update child_slot_assignments set released_at = now(), release_reason = 'archived'`, is skipped and the route returns a slotSummary that still counts the slot. The parent has no way out; the slot frees only when the deletion_purge job succeeds, and if that job exhausts its retries (max_attempts, status failed_final/dead_letter) the paid slot is consumed permanently with no parent-visible remedy.
findings.repro: Family with paid_slots = 1, child A active holding the one slot, sibling B draft. Parent requests deletion of A (POST /v1/deletion {scope:'child',childId:A} -> 202). Parent then activates B: POST /v1/children/B/activate. The capacity query returns paid_slots=1, open=1, so the route throws businessRule('NEEDS_PAID_SLOT', 'All 1 paid child slots are in use. Add a child slot to your plan first.') — a 422 telling the parent to buy a second $9.99 slot. POST /v1/children/A/archive answers 200 and changes nothing (status is already 'archived'), and POST /v1/children/A/activate answers 404.

----------

--------------------------------------+-------------+----------------

open_assignments = 1 >= paid_slots = 1 is exactly the NEEDS_PAID_SLOT branch (family.ts:362). released_at is still null after the archive route's guard would have skipped its block. `grep -rn child_slot_assignments supabase/migrations/*.sql` shows the only writers are 0200 (table/trigger), the archive route, activate, and the three purge definitions — request_deletion is absent from every version (0600, 0620, 0710, 0820, 0840).
findings.suggestedFix: Release the slot at request time, where the rest of the "stop processing immediately" work already happens: add `update public.child_slot_assignments set released_at = now(), release_reason = 'deletion' where family_id = p_family and released_at is null and (p_child is null or child_id = p_child);` to public.request_deletion in a new migration (and give release_reason's check constraint that value). Independently, make the archive route's release idempotent — move the `update child_slot_assignments ... where released_at is null` out of the `if (child.status !== 'archived')` block in apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:392 so an already-archived child with a stuck open assignment can still be reconciled.

findings.title: Lock-order inversion between the new PATCH /v1/children/:childId (families FOR UPDATE, then the child row) and POST /children/:childId/pairing-code (child row, then families via the FK) deadlocks
findings.mechanism: PATCH /v1/children/:childId takes `select 1 from public.families ... for update` (family.ts:238) and only afterwards `update public.child_profiles` (which takes FOR NO KEY UPDATE on the child row). POST /children/:childId/pairing-code does the opposite, deliberately: it takes the child row first (`for no key update`, family.ts:319, the BUG-106 fix) and then inserts into private.child_pairing_codes, whose `family_id uuid not null references public.families (id)` (migration 0001:312) makes Postgres take FOR KEY SHARE on the same families row — which FOR UPDATE blocks. The two orders are a textbook ABBA cycle, so one transaction is killed with SQLSTATE 40P01. L-021 (BUG-106) recorded that other parent-locking paths were swept and "no other inversion found", but that sweep looked at triggers, not at the FK lock the pairing-code INSERT itself takes on families. POST /children/:id/activate (family.ts:344) and POST /children/:id/archive (family.ts:388) have the same families-first order, so they are in the cycle too. app.ts:176 maps 40P01 to PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, so the victim's request answers 503 'The service is busy. Please try again.' with Retry-After: 1 — and in the repro the victim was the families-first side, i.e. the parent's profile edit / slot activation / archive, not the pairing request.
findings.repro: Two connections against the migrated schema, one family F and one child C: (A) BEGIN; select 1 from families where id=F for update; [pause]; update child_profiles set nickname='Edited' where id=C. (B) [starts during A's pause] BEGIN; select 1 from child_profiles where id=C for no key update; insert into private.child_pairing_codes (family_id, child_id, code_hash, created_by, expires_at) values (F, C, ...). B blocks on the FK's FOR KEY SHARE on F; A then blocks on C; the deadlock detector kills A.
findings.proof:
Ran the two scripts concurrently on pl_scratch_r2 (files kept at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/hunt-r4/api-family-learning/{a,b}.sql,{a,b}.out). Session A printed:

ERROR:  deadlock detected
DETAIL:  Process 20906 waits for ShareLock on transaction 3042551; blocked by process 20905.
Process 20905 waits for ShareLock on transaction 3042550; blocked by process 20906.
CONTEXT:  while locking tuple (0,1) in relation "child_profiles"

Session B printed `INSERT 0 1` / `B committed`. So the families-first transaction (PATCH/activate/archive) is the victim and answers 503.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the pairing-code transaction the same first lock as the other family writes: in apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:318-320, take `select 1 from public.families where id = ${familyId} for no key update` BEFORE the `select 1 from public.child_profiles ... for no key update`. That keeps BUG-106's invariant (child row still locked before any code row) and removes the cycle. Alternatively drop the families FOR UPDATE from PATCH /children/:childId, which only needs to serialise against activate/archive on the child row itself — but then activate and archive still need the family lock, so locking families first everywhere is the cheaper rule.

findings.title: The two new PATCH write routes have no rate limit, unlike every sibling parent write, and each one appends an audit_events row that nothing prunes
findings.mechanism: Every other parent write in these two files reserves a per-family bound before doing work: POST /children uses RATE_RULES.childCreatePerFamily (family.ts:190), POST /children/:id/pairing-code uses pairingCreatePerFamily (family.ts:282), and learning.ts gates subject/test-date/study-material creates and even the update-only PUT /learning-schedule through familyWriteLimit (scheduleUpdatePerFamily). The new PATCH /v1/family (family.ts:158) and PATCH /v1/children/:childId (family.ts:228) call neither enforceRateLimit nor familyWriteLimit, and app.ts installs no global per-user limiter. Each call writes one public.audit_events row (family.ts:176 and 254). audit_events has no Data-API hourly bound in migration 0860 (which covers child_subjects, test_dates, study_materials, learning_schedules, rewards, support_cases, support_case_messages) and no retention sweep in 0680_retention.sql, so the rows are permanent. RATE_RULES' own comment states the project rule being broken: 'Parent create routes, per family (API-AUTH-R1-04; spec: every endpoint defines a limit)'.
findings.repro: A signed-in parent with a recent adult unlock loops `PATCH /v1/family {"displayName":"a"}` (or `PATCH /v1/children/<id> {"nickname":"a"}`). Every request answers 200 and inserts one audit_events row; nothing refuses the 1000th or the 100000th, and each also takes a FOR UPDATE on the family row, serialising the family's other writes behind it.
findings.proof: Code read: `grep -n "enforceRateLimit\|familyWriteLimit" apps/api/src/routes/family.ts` shows hits only in POST /children (190) and POST /children/:id/pairing-code (282) — neither PATCH handler. `grep -n "rateLimit\|enforceRateLimit\|RATE_RULES" apps/api/src/app.ts` prints nothing, so there is no global limiter. `grep -rn audit_events supabase/migrations/0680_retention.sql supabase/migrations/0860_hardening_r2_db.sql` finds only an audit INSERT in 0680 and a comment in 0860 — no bound and no prune for that table.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a per-family rule (e.g. RATE_RULES.profileUpdatePerFamily = { limit: 30, windowSeconds: 3600 }) and call enforceRateLimit/familyWriteLimit at the top of both PATCH handlers, after currentFamilyId and before readJson, the same shape POST /children uses.

findings.title: PATCH /v1/children/:childId answers 404 'Child not found' for a child that the same API lists with deletionPending: true, so the parent is told the profile is gone
findings.mechanism: visibleChild() (family.ts:40-58) hides a child under an open deletion and its doc states the reason: 'Returns undefined for an unknown id, another family's child and a child under deletion alike, so a caller learns nothing from the difference (NOT_FOUND on every one).' That reasoning is sound for activate and pairing-code as an anti-enumeration measure, but it does not hold for the profile edit of the caller's OWN child: the same round deliberately keeps that child in GET /v1/family and marks it `deletionPending: true` (family.ts:113-125, packages/contracts/src/family.ts:79), so the response has already disclosed to this exact caller that the child exists and is under deletion. Nothing is protected by the 404, and the cost is a wrong message: the immediately adjacent archived case gets a truthful 422 businessRule('CHILD_ARCHIVED', ...) (family.ts:242-247) while the deletion-pending case claims the profile does not exist.
findings.repro: Family with children Riley and Sam. POST /v1/deletion {scope:'child', childId: Riley} -> 202. GET /v1/family -> children includes {id: Riley, nickname:'Riley', status:'archived', deletionPending:true}. PATCH /v1/children/<Riley> {gradeLevel: 7} -> 404 {error:{code:'NOT_FOUND', message:'Child not found'}}. A parent on a tab opened before the request (the web hides the control only after a refetch; apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:305) taps Save and is told the child they can still see in the list does not exist.
findings.proof: Pinned by the round's own test, apps/api/tests/family-profile.review.test.ts:254 ('refuses a profile edit while the deletion is open' expects 404) together with :295 ('keeps the child in GET /v1/family, flagged, so the privacy screens can still name it', expecting nickname 'Riley', status 'archived', deletionPending true). Both assertions pass at 8bc022b: `pnpm --filter @pencillift/api exec vitest run tests/family-profile.review.test.ts --reporter=default` -> 19 passed. So one response names the child while the other denies it exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep visibleChild() as the gate for activate and pairing-code, but in PATCH /v1/children/:childId separate the two cases: look the child up by (id, family_id) with the families deleted_at join, and when a deletion covering it is open throw a BUSINESS_RULE with a stable rule code (e.g. 'CHILD_DELETION_PENDING', message 'This child's data is being deleted, so the profile can no longer be changed'), the same shape as CHILD_ARCHIVED. An id that is unknown or another family's still answers NOT_FOUND, so nothing new is enumerable.

checkedSound: Practice-set keyset cursor round trip (learning.ts:1009-1019): `((extract(epoch from created_at)*1000000)::bigint)::text` and `timestamptz 'epoch' + $n::bigint * interval '1 microsecond'` are exact for microsecond timestamptz — verified in psql on three rows including .123456 and .000001 (roundtrip = t for all).

Practice-set page boundary with ties: seeded 35 rows sharing one created_at and replayed the route's page-1 query (order created_at desc, id desc, limit 31, slice 30), derived the cursor from the last kept row, ran the page-2 predicate — page1=30, page2=5, overlap=0, distinct_total=35. No row skipped or repeated at a tie boundary, and `order by created_at desc, id desc` matches the `(created_at, id) <` tuple direction.

cursorMicros (learning.ts:124-130) bounds: 19-digit regex values above 9223372036854775807 and anything more than ten years past the request clock are refused as 400; with that bound the largest reachable micros is ~1.8e15, well inside int64 and inside float8's exact range for `interval * bigint`, so the SQL interval multiplication cannot lose precision or overflow. The four copies of INT64_MAX/CURSOR_AHEAD_MICROS/cursorMicros (admin-ops.ts:172, homework.ts:124, privacy.ts:459, learning.ts:115) are byte-identical — no surface is missing the bound.

nextCursor emission: `limit PARENT_SET_LIMIT + 1` with `hasMore = sets.length > 30` and the extra row's items never fetched; nextCursor is null exactly when no older set exists. Worst case is one extra empty page when the total is a multiple of 30. The web consumes it (PracticeSetsSection.tsx showOlder appends `&after=`/`?after=` correctly, resets on a filter change, de-duplicates by id, and drops attached pages when the first page's cursor moves).
practice_sets.created_at is `timestamptz not null default now()` (0100_learning.sql:334), so cursor_micros can never be null and no malformed `null_<uuid>` cursor can be emitted.

Family timezone validation on PATCH /v1/family: isValidIanaZone (luxon IANAZone.isValidZone -> Intl) accepts raw offsets such as '+05:00', but the families_timezone_iana trigger (0720, `before insert or update of timezone`, fires for every role including service_role) refuses anything not in pg_timezone_names — proved in psql: `REFUSED +05:00 sqlstate=23514`, which errors.ts maps to VALIDATION_FAILED 'Invalid time zone'. Also checked the reverse gap: of all 499 pg_timezone_names entries, zero are accepted by Intl yet flagged by isFixedOffsetZone, so no storable zone silently falls back to FALLBACK_ZONE in the scheduler. A saved zone always means what GET /v1/family shows.

Timezone change and derived scheduling: enqueueDueLearningJobs (learning-jobs.ts:1728) calls rescheduleReviewJobs for every active child on every tick, and freshScheduleContext (learning-jobs.ts:1513-1522) compares the zone as well as schedule_version and reloads on a zone change, moving a job whose key is unchanged rather than cancelling it. So PATCH /v1/family not calling reschedule() itself is reconciled by the tick, not a lost plan.

22008/22007 in knownConstraintError: premise confirmed — psql shows `'0000-01-01'::date` and `'1790424000'::timestamptz` both raise 22008, so the year-0 500 the fix describes was real. Looked for an internal (non-caller) source that the new 400 would now mask without an error log, the way the comment argues for keeping 22003 a 500: the only internally built timestamp arithmetic in a route is the keyset `epoch + micros` (bounded, cannot overflow) and `(payload->>'releaseAt')::timestamptz` in /child/reviews/current, whose payload is written only as `releaseAt.toISOString()` (learning-jobs.ts:1625). No reachable masking path. pgConstraint reads postgres.js's `constraint_name`, which is the field porsager's driver sets.

calendarDateSchema / calendarMonthSchema year bound (2000..2100): swept every caller-supplied date that reaches a `::date` or month cast — learning.ts:721-722 (pause from/to), :801 (test_dates), promotions.ts:312-334 and p17-jobs (monthToDate of calendarMonthSchema), admin-monetization.ts:80 and admin-promotions.ts:42 (`month` query). All go through the bounded schemas; the only remaining bare `z.iso.date()` are a response field (monetization.ts:507) and an internal job payload (learning-jobs.ts:927). No legitimate input is excluded: no birth dates use these schemas and no far-future sentinel ('9999-…') exists anywhere in src, fixtures or SQL. Zod 4 keeps `.refine` on a string schema a string schema, so `.optional()`/`.nullable()` uses still typecheck.

deletion-pending rule coverage across every route that can reach a child row: family.ts activate (:349), pairing-code (:292) and PATCH (:240) all go through visibleChild; learning.ts ownedChild (:195-213) and ownedSet (:219-235) apply the same predicate; rewards.ts notBeingDeleted (:333-340), homework.ts:1149 and privacy.ts export request (:610-624) match. The family-scope case is genuinely covered: request_deletion (0840) sets families.deleted_at AND revokes memberships at request time, so currentFamilyId returns nothing and every one of these routes answers 404 — verified by the round's own test 'refuses activation, pairing and edits while a whole-family deletion is open'. Migration 0860's child_profiles_no_activation_under_deletion trigger backstops re-activation for every writer including service_role (42501 -> 403 in app.ts:117). Archive not using visibleChild is harmless: it only reduces access (see FL-R4-01 for the separate slot problem).

GET /v1/family flag correctness: the EXISTS is scoped to `d.family_id = c.family_id and (d.scope='family' or d.target_child_id = c.id)` with status in (requested, processing), so a sibling's request does not flag other children (test asserts Sam deletionPending false) and a completed/cancelled request does not flag at all. deletionPending is additive and optional in familyChildSchema, and both clients read it (ChildrenPage.tsx:169, mobile children.tsx). `data.family[0]!`'s non-null assertion is safe because memberships_member_read itself requires families.deleted_at is null, so currentFamilyId 404s before GET /family can see an invisible family row. The `d.scope = 'family' or` branch is consequently unreachable — dead but harmless.

PATCH route authorization and audit: both new routes resolve the family from verified membership (currentFamilyId), call assertRecentUnlock (a real `select app.has_recent_adult_unlock()` in the DB, not a token claim — so using asService does not weaken the step-up that families_member_update/child_profiles_member_update would have required), refuse a cross-family id with 404, refuse an archived child with CHILD_ARCHIVED, and write audit_events. The child audit's metadata uses `${JSON.stringify(...)}::text::jsonb` per L-006 and stores only field NAMES, never the nickname. No child_profiles uniqueness index exists, so a repeated nickname cannot produce a stray 23505.

Contracts shape: updateFamilyRequestSchema / updateChildProfileRequestSchema are strict with an at-least-one-field refine (empty body and unknown keys are 400 — pinned by the round's tests), nickname reuses freeTextSchema({max:40}) so control characters and length match POST /children exactly, gradeLevel and ageBand reuse the same K-8 / under-13 enums, and the responses are strict objects that the web and mobile both parse (childArchiveResponseSchema, updateChildProfileResponseSchema, updateFamilyResponseSchema, childActivationResponseSchema are all imported and used, none is dead).

findings.title: The new oldest-end unresolved bound does not drain for parent-filed reports, so a newer safety flag is permanently hidden from the family list
findings.mechanism: GET /v1/safety-reports (privacy.ts:761-780) now returns `unresolved` = the 200 OLDEST rows with status <> 'resolved', plus the 100 newest resolved. The comment at 122-132 justifies the oldest-end bound with "the bound drains — every report a grown-up acts on makes room for the next". That is false for reporter_kind = 'parent': the guardian action path refuses them outright (privacy.ts:815-820, PRIVACY_RULES.parentActionNotForReport), and migration 0790's safety_reports_resolution_shape only permits a resolution on 'system' and 'child' reports ("a parent's own report is closed by the reviewer"). So a parent-filed report can never leave the unresolved set through any family-facing surface — only the owner-admin queue can resolve it. Once 200 unresolved parent reports exist, every LATER system flag and every later child report falls outside the window and is absent from the response. The web portal (apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:236) and the mobile app (apps/mobile/src/privacy/parent-privacy.ts:281) build the actionable list solely from this response and PATCH per listed report, and the guardian flag email links to /app/privacy (apps/api/src/jobs/dispatcher.ts:388), so a flag outside the window is unreachable and unactionable from every product surface. This is the exact failure CS-R2-07 set out to remove (a cap hiding work a grown-up must act on), reintroduced from the other end. Reaching 200 is cheap: POST /v1/safety-reports is rate-limited at 30/hour PER USER (privacy.ts:62), so one guardian fills the window in under 7 hours and two in ~3.5 — the abuse case matters because an adult who is the subject of a child's disclosure can pre-fill the window so that future flags on that child never appear in the family list.
findings.repro: 1. Guardian A posts 200 reports to POST /v1/safety-reports (30/hour). All land status='open', reporter_kind='parent'. 2. The scan job then files a system flag on a child's answer (status='escalated', family_visible=true) and enqueues safety_flag_email. 3. GET /v1/safety-reports as either guardian: the 200 older open parent rows fill the unresolved CTE; the flag is not in `reports`. 4. The guardian receives the email, opens /app/privacy, sees no flag. PATCH /v1/safety-reports/:id on any of the 200 parent rows returns 422 parentActionNotForReport, so nothing they can do frees a slot.

Printed: `returned=200 | system_flag_listed=f | child_report_listed=f`. Code proof of the non-draining half: privacy.ts:815-820 throws businessRule(parentActionNotForReport) for reporter_kind='parent', and supabase/migrations/0790_parent_flag_review.sql:33-42 forbids any resolution on a parent report. The round's own test acknowledges the gap by resolving the filler rows with raw SQL instead of the action path — apps/api/tests/privacy-r2.review.test.ts:624-626 "(the query is what is under test here, not the action path)" — and its only flag-visibility case puts the flag OLDER than the filler rows, so the newer-flag case is untested.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not let rows the family cannot act on consume the bound. Either (a) partition the list: always return every report the family can act on (reporter_kind in ('system','child') and status <> 'resolved') with no cap or with keyset paging (BUG-117), and cap the guardian's own pending reports separately; or (b) order the unresolved CTE by actionability first — `order by (reporter_kind = 'parent'), created_at asc` — so parent rows are the ones squeezed out, never a system flag. Either way add an API test whose flag is NEWER than UNRESOLVED_REPORTS_PAGE_SIZE unresolved parent reports.

findings.title: The new family_data export ships the child's safety-notice body, which encodes which kind of concern was flagged
findings.mechanism: CS-R2-05 added `childFeedback: select id, question_id, child_id, kind, body, created_at from public.child_feedback where family_id = ...` to the 'family_data' export with no filter on `kind`, so every row with kind='safety' is exported verbatim. That body is childSafetyMessage(screen.categories, ageBand) (packages/domain/src/safety/templates.ts:137-151), and its composition is a pure function of the screen categories: a self_harm flag adds the 988 line, an abuse/sexual/secrecy/personal_contact flag adds the Childhelp 1-800-422-4453 line and suppresses the anger line, a violence-only flag adds the anger line. Twelve lines below, the same commit's `safetyFlags` block claims the opposite guarantee — "no category, no screen_categories, no screen_version and no provider codes, so the export cannot say which kind of concern was flagged (CS-R2-02)" (export-build.ts:529-532) — while still exporting `feedback_id`, which joins each flag to the exact notice row. So the round-3 fix that removed the screen codes from the family-readable audit row (apps/api/src/jobs/scan-process.ts:2219-2250, which correctly writes the reviewer-only row with family_id = null) is defeated by the sibling surface the same round opened. This breaks the project rule that the family never learns WHICH KIND of safety concern, and it matters most in the case the design exists for: the adult who reads the export may be the subject of the child's disclosure. It also now covers provider-only flags, since CS-R2-03 made an unmapped provider category fall back to violence+abuse (packages/ai/src/moderation.ts:128, 216-220), i.e. the Childhelp wording.
findings.repro: 1. A child's answer screens severe as self_harm on one question and as abuse on another; the scan job writes two child_feedback rows kind='safety' and two system reports. 2. Any guardian: POST /v1/exports {kind:'family_data'} after a PIN unlock, wait for export_build, download the JSON. 3. childFeedback[] contains both bodies; the one carrying "call or text 988" is the self-harm flag and the one carrying "Childhelp hotline at 1-800-422-4453" is the abuse-type flag, and safetyFlags[].feedback_id names which flag each belongs to.

Add an API test on the built family_data JSON asserting that no exported string contains '988' or '422-4453' when a flag exists, next to the existing CS-R2-02 audit-row test.

findings.title: A scan stopped by consent withdrawal is explained to the parent as bad photos, and the advice it gives cannot work
findings.mechanism: settleScansAfterConsentWithdrawal (guardians.ts:84-123, new this round) ends every queued/extracting/checking initial scan as status='failed_final', error_code='CONSENT_REQUIRED'. The parent portal maps failed_final error codes in FAILED_FINAL_COPY (apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.tsx:126-134), which this round extended for the two codes the jobs fix introduced (SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS, AI_PAUSED_TOO_LONG) but has no line for CONSENT_REQUIRED, so explainStatus falls back to the state copy at HomeworkPage.tsx:110-112: "This scan could not be processed after several tries. Please start a new scan with clear photos." Neither clause is true — the scan was stopped once, by the family's own withdrawal, and the photos were fine — and the action it recommends cannot succeed: a new upload re-checks consent and is refused with the 422 business rule CONSENT_REQUIRED (packages/contracts/src/homework.ts:226). The copy also stays silent about the one good fact the settlement does deliver, that the page allowance was released (guardians.ts:116-119). The code was already reachable through the job's own assertActive path before this round, but the new settlement makes it the normal outcome for every pending scan at withdrawal rather than a rare race.
findings.repro: 1. A family with verified consent uploads a scan; the scan_process job is queued (assignment status 'queued'). 2. POST /v1/consent/withdraw with a recent PIN unlock. 3. The job is cancelled and the assignment becomes failed_final / CONSENT_REQUIRED. 4. Open the homework list in the portal: the scan reads "Could not finish — This scan could not be processed after several tries. Please start a new scan with clear photos." 5. Following that advice, a new scan upload is refused 422 CONSENT_REQUIRED.
findings.proof: Read-only inspection: guardians.ts:89 (`const CODE = 'CONSENT_REQUIRED'`) and 115 (`await move('failed_final')`); HomeworkPage.tsx:126-134 lists only FORMAT_NEEDS_CONVERSION, SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS and AI_PAUSED_TOO_LONG, and explainStatus (HomeworkPage.tsx:135-144) falls back to STATUS_COPY.failed_final (108-112). `grep -rn "CONSENT_REQUIRED" apps/web/src` returns no hit, so no other web surface supplies the wording.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a FAILED_FINAL_COPY line for CONSENT_REQUIRED (and mirror it in the mobile homework copy): say that checking stopped because parental consent was withdrawn, that the pages were given back / the allowance released, and that consent must be given again before a new scan — not "start a new scan with clear photos".

checkedSound: packages/ai/src/moderation.ts fail-closed screen (CS-R2-03): providerSafetyScreen now returns level 'severe' for every moderationFlagged() item, and a flag with no category or with only unknown names takes PROVIDER_FALLBACK_CATEGORY; the two fallback paths (providerSafetyCategories' per-name fallback and the empty-categories branch at 216-220) agree, addMapped adds 'abuse' only for source 'child', and both fallback categories are inside migration 0760's allowed six, so the report insert's `screen_categories <@ array[...]` and `cardinality between 1 and 6` checks cannot be violated by the fallback. The harassment/hate/illicit remap and the abuse-wording consequence are recorded owner/lead decisions (moderation.ts:92-100, 120-127) with the precision cost stated, so not reported.

providerSafetyScreen is only wired for the child's own answers (scan-process.ts:566 childInputScreen); model output fails closed on moderationFlagged() directly in moderatedCoaching and moderatedCriteria, and both treat a moderation failure as 'drop the output', so no model text reaches a child unmoderated.

Consent/ZDR gate before the moderation call: ScanRun.moderate (scan-process.ts:1084-1109) runs assertActive (verified consent, live family, no pending deletion, child not archived) and checkChildDataGate before any provider call, and returns MODERATION_NOT_AVAILABLE non-retryably when the gate refuses; screenBeforeGrading then grades nothing and throws (2117-2124).

screenBeforeGrading fail-closed ordering: with a failed moderation call the word-list severe questions are still answered (template + report, filed visible with providerModeration:'unavailable' in the audit row), a cleared question is skipped rather than graded, and the run always throws afterwards, so no question is graded on the word list alone.

The reviewer-only audit row (CS-R2-02): audit_events.family_id is nullable with no target_type constraint (0001:401-412), so the insert cannot raise; audit_member_read (0001:520-522) requires `family_id is not null` for a family member, so the screenCategories/providerCodes row is unreadable by any family member through the Data API, and the family-visible row carries only category 'severe_risk' and screenVersion. No API route reads audit_events at all, and app.prevent_mutation blocks deletes, so no purge/retention interaction. The family/reviewer split follows the same `held` decision as safety_reports.family_visible.

The clearance re-check key (CS-R2-01/L-033): `coalesce(max(substring(idempotency_key from ':v([0-9]+)$')::int),0)+1` over `scan:<assignmentId>:v%` is retention-proof — verified in psql that a set {v2,v10,vX,v3-retry} yields 10, so a pruned v1 with a surviving v2 produces v11, never a colliding v2. homework.ts:1018 and 1388 use the identical form, so the sibling surfaces agree; the usage_reservations key `scan-usage:<id>:v<count+1>` is still count-derived but those rows are deleted only by the child/family purge, which removes the assignment too.

Consent-withdrawal settlement (CS-R2-04) mechanics: every status step it performs is permitted by app.guard_assignment_transition (0100:102-128) — queued->extracting, extracting/checking/verifying/failed_retryable->failed_final, checking/verifying->needs_parent_review; release_reason 'failed_final' is in the usage_reservations check list (0200:208) and status='released' satisfies the paired check; the reservation key pattern matches what homework.ts writes; it is idempotent when two jobs (v1 failed_retryable + v2 queued) name the same assignment because the second pass sees failed_final; it mirrors settleDeadLetteredScan exactly; and it locks jobs then assignments, the same order as the dispatcher, so no new deadlock. safety_flag_email stays in JOBS_KEPT_ON_CONSENT_WITHDRAWAL, so a flag filed before the withdrawal is still emailed.

No clock mixing in the flag/transcription keys: safety_reports.transcription_at is read in SQL from coalesce(q.corrected_at, q.created_at), extracted_questions.corrected_at is written as SQL now() (homework.ts:1379), and child_feedback.created_at defaults to now(), so the `created_at >= coalesce(corrected_at, -infinity)` replay guards in safetyResponse/keepSafetyNotice/rubricFeedback compare one clock. The guardian PATCH's app-clock parent_action_at/resolved_at are never compared against a DB instant.

Partial-clearance behaviour is consistent across surfaces: screenBeforeGrading's cleared_now/all_cleared (scan-process.ts:2050-2066) and the child assignment route's safety_cleared (homework.ts:1499-1506) use the same two-EXISTS shape, so the notice stays until the last system report on the question is cleared and a cleared question is graded only when all are. safety_reports and child_feedback are never pruned by any retention sweep (only by the deletion purge), so neither derived flag can flip because rows aged out.

The family report list's other properties: the response is bounded at 300 rows, unresolved sorts before resolved (`order by (status <> 'resolved') desc`) and no CTE names family_visible or screen_categories, so RLS plus the 0760 column grants still keep the screen codes and any held report out; safetyReportsResponseSchema has no array max, so the larger page cannot break the client parse the way the admin schema's .max would.

The admin queue's keyset paging (privacy.ts:913-955) is oldest-first with a cursor and a BigInt-validated `after`, so no escalated report becomes unreachable there; ADMIN_COLUMNS never selects note text, and the round-3 falseMatchNotReleasable guard (1000-1005) still blocks releasing a cleared held flag.

Guardian PATCH /safety-reports/:id: scoped to the caller's family and family_visible under a row lock, refuses a resolved report (409), refuses false_match on anything but a system report with a question, requires a recent PIN unlock, refuses the clearance while the scan is mid-run (lockFlaggedScan/SCAN_STILL_CHECKING), and writes only ids/codes to the audit row. No DB constraint in 0790 requires a resolution_note for this path, so the write cannot fail on the constraint.

safetyResponse idempotency: the child notice and the report are written in one guardedWrite with `on conflict (question_id, transcription_at) where reporter_kind='system' do nothing`, and the safety_flag_email job is inserted in the same transaction as the report, so a replay adds neither a duplicate report nor a second email. providerModerationCodes emits only [A-Z0-9_] slugs capped at 40 characters, so nothing text-like reaches the audit metadata or the logs (the COUNT of codes is bounded only by the provider's response, which I could not show ever exceeding 13 categories).
